# The official-news pack

*Official news* · version 1.0.0 · code `ONEWS`

## What it is

Press releases and notices from the publishers' own feeds: the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the Bank of Canada, the Bank of England, the SEC, OSFI, the US Federal Register and the Canada Gazette. A publisher's page lists its latest releases newest first, each a link to the original, with its terms; a release's page gives its title, date, summary and link. Each publisher's terms are recorded: the Bank of England, OSFI and the Canada Gazette allow no commercial reuse, so their releases are internal only. Filled daily by the official-news feed into the newslake lake.

## Data structures

Every kind the pack owns, read from its manifest, its samples and its Sutras: how its ids look, its fields (type, an example, what it means), its nested lists and the fields that link to other kinds. A path `A[].B` is field `B` of every element of list `A`.

### `release-source`

**Official press releases** · mnemonic `PRESS` · read through connector `officialnews-store`.

**Id:** field `SOURCE_ID`; pattern `^PRESS-`; for example `PRESS-BOC`.

Fields, from 9 sample documents:

| Field | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BY_CATEGORY` | list of objects |  | The kept releases counted by category (CATEGORY, COUNT), the largest first. |
| `COUNTRY` | string | `CAN` | The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the publisher's country (EMU for the euro area). |
| `FEED_URL` | string | `https://www.bankofcanada.ca/content_type…` | The address the feed reads (RSS, Atom, or the Federal Register's API). |
| `INTERNAL_ONLY` | boolean | `false` | True when the publisher's terms allow no commercial reuse: the record stays inside the organisation (Export data refuses it). |
| `LAST_PUBLISHED` | timestamp | `2026-11-16T10:00:04Z` | When the newest kept release was published (UTC). |
| `LAST_PULL` | string | `ok` | ok, or failed (the kept releases are shown) when the publisher's feed could not be read. |
| `LATEST` | list of objects |  | The newest 25 releases, newest first: PUBLISHED, TITLE, URL, CATEGORY and PRESS_RELEASE. |
| `LICENCE` | string | `Bank of Canada terms of use: free to use…` | The publisher's terms of reuse, as recorded in the feed's YAML. |
| `NAME` | string | `Bank of Canada` | The publisher's name. |
| `PROVENANCE` | object |  | Where the record comes from, one object: SOURCE, DATASET, RETRIEVED_AT, LICENCE, ATTRIBUTION, URL and INTERNAL_ONLY. |
| `PUBLISHER_TYPE` | string | `central bank` | What the publisher is. |
| `RELEASES` | integer | `6` | How many releases are kept (the last keep-days, at most keep-per-source). |
| `SOURCE_ID` | string | `PRESS-BOC` | PRESS- and the publisher's id in the feed's YAML (FED, ECB, BOC, BOE, SEC, OSFI, FEDREG, GAZETTE1, GAZETTE2). |
| `TERMS_URL` | string | `https://www.bankofcanada.ca/terms/` | The publisher's terms page. |
| `WEBSITE` | string | `https://www.bankofcanada.ca/press/press-…` | The publisher's page of releases. |
| `WHY_INTERNAL` | string | `The Bank of England allows personal and …` | Why the publisher's releases are internal only, in words; empty when they are not. |

Nested structures:

| Path | Fields |
|---|---|
| `BY_CATEGORY[]` | `CATEGORY` (string): The category, Uncategorised when the feed gives none., `COUNT` (integer): How many kept releases have that category. |
| `LATEST[]` | `CATEGORY` (string): The publisher's category for it, where its feed gives one., `PRESS_RELEASE` (string): The release's page in Drishti (PREL-...)., `PUBLISHED` (timestamp): When the release was published (UTC)., `TITLE` (string): The release's title., `URL` (string): The release on the publisher's site. |
| `PROVENANCE` | `ATTRIBUTION` (string): The credit line to repeat when the release is shown or republished., `DATASET` (string): The publisher's feed the record was read from., `INTERNAL_ONLY` (boolean): True when the publisher's terms allow no commercial reuse: the record stays inside the organisation (Export data refuses it)., `LICENCE` (string): The publisher's terms of reuse, as recorded in the feed's YAML., `RETRIEVED_AT` (date): The business date of the feed's pull that wrote the record., `SOURCE` (string): The publisher., `URL` (string): The original on the publisher's site. |

| Path | Fields |

| `PROVENANCE` | `ATTRIBUTION` (string): The credit line to repeat when the release is shown or republished., `DATASET` (string): The publisher's feed the record was read from., `INTERNAL_ONLY` (boolean): True when the publisher's terms allow no commercial reuse: the record stays inside the organisation (Export data refuses it)., `LICENCE` (string): The publisher's terms of reuse, as recorded in the feed's YAML., `RETRIEVED_AT` (date): The business date of the feed's pull that wrote the record., `SOURCE` (string): The publisher., `URL` (string): The original on the publisher's site. |

## Refreshing the data

The **official-news** feed (`config/feeds/official-news.yaml`: its sources and their licences in `options.sources`, its schedule, daily at 19:00 local time, and its selection in `options`) pulls what is new into `<data>/datafeeds/official-news/<date>/` and loads it into the `newslake` lake: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news` (the parallel loader), `--load inbox` (the server's data inbox loads it), `--dry-run` (what it would ask). With the Python you run Drishti with: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news` on Linux and macOS, `py -3.13 tools\drishti.py feed run official-news` on Windows; the schedule for cron, systemd or Task Scheduler: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed schedule`. It needs no key. The pack's data is its committed snapshot, `data/testdata/official-news/<kind>/`, from a live run: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news --snapshot` pulls the latest data and rewrites it, with the pack's reference samples (a few documents of each kind for this README and the docs, never served) and this README; `python3 tools/drishti.py lake demo` builds the snapshot into the lake the connector reads.

The data feed `official-news` (config/feeds/official-news.yaml) pulls `release-source`, `press-release`: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news` fetches them daily into `data/datafeeds/official-news/<date>/` and loads them into the lake `newslake`; `--dry-run` says what it would fetch, changing nothing; `--snapshot` refreshes the committed snapshot in data/testdata instead; `feed status` shows the last runs. The External data feeds guide (docs/guides/WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md) has the schedule entries for Linux and Windows.

The pack's files are written by `tools/packgen/publicsector/make.py`; its `--check` fails when the committed files differ from what it would write.

## Data contracts

Every kind of the pack has a data contract: a YAML file beside the pack (`modules/news-and-events/packs/official-news/contracts/<kind>.contract.yaml`, checked against `tools/contracts.schema.json`) that says what one record is, its key, how it is stored and dated, and every field with its type, presence, unit and meaning. The contracts are published on [docs/contracts/packs/official-news.md](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/official-news.md) and each kind's example (a real record of the test data, every field explained) on [docs/contracts/packs](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/README.md); this README links them and copies neither. Check them against the pack and its data with `python3 tools/contracts.py check` (or `drishti.py contract check`); show one with `python3 tools/contracts.py show <MNEMONIC>`.

| Command | Kind | Class | Key | Grain | Contract | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PRESS` | `release-source` | fundamental | `SOURCE_ID` | One row per official press releases, keyed by SOURCE_ID. | [PRESS: Official press releases](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/official-news.md#press-official-press-releases-release-source) (`contracts/release-source.contract.yaml`) | [example](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/official-news.md#example-official-news-release-source) |
| `PREL` | `press-release` | fundamental | `RELEASE_ID` | One row per press release, keyed by RELEASE_ID. | [PREL: Press release](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/official-news.md#prel-press-release-press-release) (`contracts/press-release.contract.yaml`) | [example](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/official-news.md#example-official-news-press-release) |

*Class*: **fundamental** data is delivered by a source system and stored; **input** is stored data an engine reads; **computed** is worked out by Drishti when asked and never stored by a source; **drishti-owned** is kept by Drishti itself.

## Data retrieval

Where each kind's data comes from, how it reaches the lake and how to check it. Three origins: **external** data, fetched from a public source by its data feed (each source, its licence and worked examples on the [External data](../../../../docs/guides/WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md) help page); **synthetic** test data (or hand-written reference data), written by a generator with fictitious names; **computed** by a Drishti engine when it is asked, never stored by a source.

| Command | Kind | Origin | How it reaches Drishti |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRESS` | `release-source` | external: Press releases of the Federal Reserve, the SEC and the US Federal Register (RSS, API) (public domain (US Government works)); Press releases of the European Central Bank and the Bank of Canada (RSS) (free reuse with the source acknowledged); News of the Bank of England and OSFI, the Canada Gazette (RSS) (non-commercial or internal use only without permission; **internal only**) — refreshed by `drishti.py feed run official-news` | the daily feed `official-news` → `<data>/delta/newslake/officialnews/release-source/` (lake `newslake`) → connector `officialnews-store`; the committed snapshot `data/testdata/official-news/release-source/` (9 documents, retrieved 2026-11-27) → `lake demo` → the lake `newslake`, same connector |
| `PREL` | `press-release` | external: Press releases of the Federal Reserve, the SEC and the US Federal Register (RSS, API) (public domain (US Government works)); Press releases of the European Central Bank and the Bank of Canada (RSS) (free reuse with the source acknowledged); News of the Bank of England and OSFI, the Canada Gazette (RSS) (non-commercial or internal use only without permission; **internal only**) — refreshed by `drishti.py feed run official-news` | the daily feed `official-news` → `<data>/delta/newslake/officialnews/press-release/` (lake `newslake`) → connector `officialnews-store`; the committed snapshot `data/testdata/official-news/press-release/` (196 documents, retrieved 2026-11-27) → `lake demo` → the lake `newslake`, same connector |

### External sources

| Source | Where | Licence | Internal only | Refresh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Press releases of the Federal Reserve, the SEC and the US Federal Register (RSS, API) | https://www.federalreserve.gov/feeds/press_all.xml | public domain (US Government works) | no | `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news` |
| Press releases of the European Central Bank and the Bank of Canada (RSS) | https://www.ecb.europa.eu/rss/press.html | free reuse with the source acknowledged | no | `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news` |
| News of the Bank of England and OSFI, the Canada Gazette (RSS) | https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/news | non-commercial or internal use only without permission | **yes** | `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news` |

**Internal only:** News of the Bank of England and OSFI, the Canada Gazette (RSS). The terms restrict reuse or forbid redistribution: the data is for internal demonstrations only, never written into a committed folder without `--internal-ok`, and must be raised with the owner before any client or external use.

Run these from the Drishti folder (the repository root, or the install folder of a release).

```bash
python3 tools/drishti.py feed status official-news            # its last runs: last success, rows, failures (offline: the run ledger)
python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news --dry-run     # what would be fetched and loaded; changes nothing
python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news               # pull today's data and load it into the lake `newslake` (what the daily schedule runs)
python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news --load inbox  # the same through the data inbox: the server loads it
```

The same with the Python you run Drishti with: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run official-news` on Linux and macOS, `py tools\drishti.py feed run official-news` on Windows (every argument is passed on); the daily schedule entries: `drishti.py feed schedule --cron` (or `--systemd`, `--windows`) ([WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md](../../../../docs/guides/WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md)).

### Into the lake, checking, offline

- **The lake.** `python3 tools/drishti.py lake demo` reads `data/testdata/testdata.yaml` and writes every dataset (test data, the committed public-data snapshots) into `<data>/delta/<domain>/<kind>/`, where the pack's Delta connector serves it; a computed kind needs nothing loaded. `lake build` loads your own large JSON exports the same way ([Command line](../../../../docs/guides/CLI_REFERENCE.md)).
- **Checking.** `python3 tools/contracts.py check` compares every contract with the pack and its data; each generator's `--check` (above) fails when the committed files differ from what it would write; in the console, `<MNEMONIC> <GO>` lists a kind and the pack's code opens its overview with the count of each kind.
- **Offline.** Everything committed works without a network: the test data and the public-data snapshots are in the repository and `lake demo` reads only them. A data feed runs offline from its download cache (`--offline`); a connector that reaches the internet (news, yfinance, the public-data feeds) is off as shipped and never starts on a machine configured offline (`drishti.offline.plugins`).
